function: Learned joint control of UAV excitation current weights (collaborative beamforming) and UAV positions to maximize secrecy rate against a mobile eavesdropper while minimizing flight energy (pp. 6-7)
system: A2G link: 8 single-antenna UAVs (0.1 W each) form a virtual array to a remote BS at 2.4 GHz; mobile eavesdropper; no RIS (pp. 6, 11)
method: Reinforcement learning: TD3 with a diffusion-model actor (GDMTD3) and twin critics, trained in a simulated environment with a replay buffer; 4 denoising steps, 8000 episodes (pp. 8-12)
data_channel: No dataset; custom simulator: elevation-dependent probabilistic LoS air-to-ground model (ref. 37) with LoS/NLoS excess path loss; Gauss-Markov eavesdropper mobility; no 3GPP model (pp. 5, 11)
test_conditions: Trained and evaluated in one simulated environment (8 UAVs, 40 m x 40 m, mobile eavesdropper); 4-16 UAVs, seeds and denoising steps are separate simulation sweeps (pp. 11, 13-14)
baselines: Non-learned: random strategy; linear, planar and circular antenna-array deployments. Learned: DDPG, TD3, SAC, PPO, transformer-based TD3 (pp. 12-13)
metrics: Average secrecy rate per step (bps/Hz); average flight energy consumption per step (J); reward per episode (pp. 13-14)
complexity: Order of complexity: training O(4|theta_Q1|+2|theta_d|+MNT|theta_d|+MNV+...), execution O(MNT|theta_d|), space O(|theta_d|), theta = network parameters (p. 10)
q1_support: p. 5: "we utilize the elevation angle-dependent probabilistic LoS model [37]". Custom A2G simulator (LoS probability plus free-space path loss); no 3GPP TR 38.811/38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 14: "we performed a detailed simulation under varying numbers of UAVs". Each setting (UAV number, seed, denoising steps) is a separate sweep; the paper never states that a trained model is tested on an unseen scenario, UAV number or site.
q3_support: p. 12: "we also compare the proposed GDMTD3 with four well-known DRL benchmarks: DDPG, TD3, SAC [55], and PPO [56]"; non-learned random and fixed-array deployments are also compared. p. 13: "GDMTD3 achieves the highest average secrecy rate of the system".
q4_support: p. 10: "we analyze the computational and space complexity of GDMTD3 during training and execution phases". The section gives training, execution and space complexity orders in terms of network parameters, episodes M, steps N and denoising steps T.
q5_support: p. 11: "For our deep learning computations, we use PyTorch 2.2.2, along with the CUDA 11.8". The environment is a custom simulation; no code or data link and no public channel dataset is given anywhere.
notes: PDF is arXiv v1 (12 Jul 2024, p. 1) of the TMC paper; the DOI is not printed in the file, but title and authors match. Area 6: the DRL agent controls beam weights and positions of a UAV-swarm air-to-ground link. UAV positions are above the physical layer, but they are learned jointly with the beam weights (p. 7: action a[n] = (I[n], q[n])), so the above_phy rule lets it pass. The secrecy-rate objective is physical-layer security, which is not a listed excluded function. q2: the 4-16 UAV sweep (Fig. 9 on p. 15, discussed on p. 14) changes the action dimension and the paper does not say a trained model is reused. q1: the Al-Hourani probabilistic LoS model is neither 3GPP nor a public dataset.
